Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (2025) • Ministry: Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) • Total Outlay: ₹22,919 crore (including administrative expenses) • Launch Year: 2025 • Objective: o Boost domestic manufacturing of electronic components and sub-assemblies. o Increase domestic value addition and reduce import dependency. o Integrate India’s electronics industry with global value chains (GVCs). o Create employment opportunities in the manufacturing sector.

# Page 5^page=5
Key Features: • Types of Incentives: o Turnover-linked incentive: a % of incremental sales over base year. o Capex incentive: a % of eligible capital expenditure. o Hybrid incentive: Combination of turnover and capex incentive. • Target Segments: o Sub-assemblies: Display modules, camera modules. o Bare Components: Non-SMD passive components, Electro-mechanical parts, Multi-layer PCBs, Li-ion cells (excluding storage & mobility), Enclosures. o Selected Bare Components: HDI / MSAP / Flexible PCBs, SMD passive components. o Supply Chain & Capital Equipment: Components and machinery used in electronics manufacturing.

# Page 6^page=6
• Eligibility: o Both greenfield (new) and brownfield (existing) investments. o Separate applications for each product category. • Duration: o Incentives applicable for 6 years with a possible 1-year gestation period (optional basis). o Applications open from May 1, 2025, initially for 2 years (for capital goods and supply chain segments). • Performance Criteria: o Linked to incremental investment, turnover, and employment creation. o Base year for calculation: FY 2024–25. • Governance Mechanism: o Nodal agency to implement scheme. o Project Management Agency (PMA) for application processing. o Inter-Ministerial Governing Council (GC) for evaluation and approval.

Q.) Consider the following statements regarding the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS): 1. The ECMS aims to increase Domestic Value Addition (DVA) and integrate Indian firms with Global Value Chains (GVCs). 2. The scheme offers uniform incentives to all eligible applicants in the form of a flat turnover-linked subsidy. 3. As of FY 2024-25, electronics became the third-largest exported commodity from India. Which of the above statements is/are correct? A. 1 only B. 1 and 3 only C. 2 and 3 only D. 3 only E. 1, 2 and 3
